subject: Feature ROI & token budget alignment — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Priya Reddy <priya@healthsync.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Evans <tom.evans@healthsync.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + short demo — token volumes and budget

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the call today — good conversation. Quick recap and what we need next from Redwood: 

- Scope: two features under evaluation: (A) ‘Summary at a glance’ (read-only, short summaries) and (B) ‘Doctor assistant’ (structured note drafting).
- Ballpark usage (conservative): Summary: 15,000 DAU x ~8 calls/month = ~1.2M calls/month. Assistant: 2,000 DAU x ~20 calls/month = ~40k calls/month.
- Token assumptions: summary ~600 tokens/call, assistant ~2,200 tokens/call.
- Finance target: variable inference cost target of roughly $12–18 per 1M tokens (our current internal inference vendor is ~ $30/1M).
- Business ask: deliver a short feature-level P&L showing $/feature (monthly and annualized), CAC payback under 9–12 months, and margin sensitivity versus inference cost assumptions. Also show committed-volume pricing scenarios that get us into the target cost range.

Can you send a concise scenario matrix (spread across 3 inference-cost points and 2 commitment tiers) and call out any risky model-behavior items we should test in the pilot?

We’d like that before our internal budget sync on Tuesday.

Best,
Priya
Head of Product, HealthSync

--
Attachments: product_brief.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Reddy <priya@healthsync.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Feature ROI & token budget alignment — follow-up and next steps

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear ask and the token estimates, that helps a lot. Attaching two artifacts: 1) a compact XLS with the scenario matrix you requested, and 2) a short PDF that maps commitments to per-1M-token pricing ranges and expected $/feature. High-level notes below.

Quick summary of our approach in the attached:
- We modeled three per-1M-token inference cost assumptions (High: $30, Mid: $18, Low: $9) and two commitment tiers (pilot: 1–5M tokens/month, committed: 10–50M tokens/month).
- For your token mix (summary-heavy), the combined per-month token load sits around ~1.2M*600 + 40k*2200 = ~1.2B tokens/month (note: re-check arithmetic in sheet; I also include conservative 30% sampling rate for summary to reflect UI-driven calls).
- $/feature (monthly) example under Mid ($18/1M): Summary feature variable inference cost ≈ $13k/month; Assistant ≈ $1580/month. These figures assume no additional caching — we’ve also included a ‘with prefix caching’ column which drops summary cost by ~35% in typical flows.
- CAC payback: with your stated monetization plan and an assumed LTV/ACV ratio (details in sheet), payback for the initial pilot cohort is ~10 months at Mid pricing, ~6 months at Low-tier pricing.

Open questions for you to confirm so we can finalize the scenarios:
1) Can you confirm expected percentage of summary calls that will hit cache (UI-repeat calls)? Even 20% vs 50% materially shifts cost.
2) Do you anticipate prioritizing latency SLOs (P95 < 250ms) for the assistant feature? Higher latency SLOs reduce batching/cost efficiency.
3) Is there internal resistance on committing to a 12–24 month reserved contract vs month-to-month pilot?

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll drop the XLS/PDF now, and if helpful we can set a 30-min model walkthrough tomorrow.
- If the scenarios look reasonable, we’ll work up a pilot quote with a commitment-based break that hits your $12–18/1M target.

Thanks — Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: healthsync_token_estimates.xlsx (attachment stub); redwood_price-scenarios.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Priya Reddy <priya@healthsync.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Feature ROI & token budget alignment — internal pricing guidance

Looping in a quick pricing/ops note. Priya — copying for transparency.

Ben’s scenarios are good directionally. Two operational levers we should call out explicitly in the pilot quote that materially change $/1M tokens:
- Aggressive prefix and KV caching for the summary flow (we can include policy to cache top-50 phrases per cohort). If HealthSync can tolerate slightly stale summaries for 10–15s window, expectation is ~30–45% token reduction in practice.
- A model-fallback policy: use a cheaper distilled model for preview summaries and warm-up requests, fall back to the higher-quality model for final render or assistant completions. This often halves effective cost for summary-type workloads.

From a commercial perspective, if HealthSync can commit to a 12-month minimum with a 12M token/mo floor, we can underwrite an $11/1M token effective rate for the blended mix (pilot pricing ladder in the attached sheet). We’ll call out the precise SLA and change-control language in the quote.

Ben — I’m happy to join the walkthrough and surface the commitment language if we get to pilot sign-off.

Marissa
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Priya Reddy <priya@healthsync.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Evans <tom.evans@healthsync.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-20T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Feature ROI & token budget alignment — follow-up and next steps

Ben/Marissa — this is very helpful, thank you. Two quick confirmations from our side: 

1) Caching: we expect ~30% cache hit for summary initially, with scope to improve after UX tweaks — so use the ‘with caching’ column as the primary scenario.
2) Commitment: Finance is comfortable exploring a 12-month commitment if the blended effective inference cost is <= $14/1M tokens.

Next steps: please share the finalized scenario sheet and a short pilot quote (including SLAs and trial volume floor) by end of day Monday so we can review with Finance on Tuesday. Also flag any data privacy checklist items we’ll need for a pilot.

— Priya
Head of Product, HealthSync
